title: A Laconic Answer
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from "A Laconic Answer" in Fifty Famous Stories Retold by James Baldwin (1896), via Project Gutenberg. Syllable-break hyphens from the original edition's typesetting (e.g., "Spar-tans," "Mac-e-don") have been corrected.
body: Many miles beyond Rome there was a famous country which we call Greece. The people of Greece were not united like the Romans; but instead there were several states, each of which had its own rulers.

Some of the people in the southern part of the country were called Spartans, and they were noted for their simple habits and their bravery. The name of their land was Laconia, and so they were sometimes called Lacons.

One of the strange rules which the Spartans had, was that they should speak briefly, and never use more words than were needed. And so a short answer is often spoken of as being laconic; that is, as being such an answer as a Lacon would be likely to give.
There was in the northern part of Greece a land called Macedon; and this land was at one time ruled over by a warlike king named Philip.

Philip of Macedon wanted to become the master of all Greece. So he raised a great army, and made war upon the other states, until nearly all of them were forced to call him their king. Then he sent a letter to the Spartans in Laconia, and said, "If I go down into your country, I will level your great city to the ground."
In a few days, an answer was brought back to him. When he opened the letter, he found only one word written there.
It was as much as to say, "We are not afraid of you so long as the little word 'if' stands in your way."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the Spartans noted for?
options: Their skill at building ships
Their wealth and fine palaces
Their simple habits and their bravery
Their large trading fleet

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the name of the Spartans' own land?
options: Laconia
Macedon
Attica
Thessaly

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what strange rule did the Spartans have about speaking?
options: They should never speak to strangers at all
They should always speak in rhyme
They should let their king speak for them
They should speak briefly and never use more words than needed

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the name of the warlike king of Macedon?
options: Alexander
Philip
Leonidas
Pericles

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to nearly all the other Greek states because of Philip's wars?
options: They formed an alliance against Macedon
They fled across the sea to safety
They were forced to call him their king
They were left completely untouched

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Philip threaten to do in his letter to the Spartans?
options: Level their great city to the ground
Take all their ships and soldiers
Force their king to serve in his army
Burn their fields before winter

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what single word did the Spartans write back to Philip?
options: "NEVER"
"COME"
"NO"
"IF"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Spartans' one-word reply count as a truly "laconic" answer?
options: It repeats Philip's own words back to him
It uses no more words than are needed, exactly as their custom demanded
It is written in a foreign language Philip cannot read
It takes several days to compose

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the single word "IF" communicate to Philip?
options: That they agree to surrender the city at once
That they do not understand his letter
That his threat depends on an uncertainty they are not afraid of
That they want more time before answering

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the passage?
options: A brief, pointed reply can answer a threat as well as a long one
Only a large army can ever answer a king's threat
Sparta eventually surrendered its city to Philip
Greece was united under a single ruler before Philip's wars

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how was Greece different from Rome?
options: It had no cities of its own
It was ruled entirely by Sparta
It had no name for itself at the time
It was not united; it had several states with their own rulers

questions.prompt: According to the passage, in which part of Greece was Macedon located?
options: The southern part
The northern part
The eastern coast
An island offshore

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Philip do before sending his letter to the Spartans?
options: He asked the Spartans to join his army
He gave up his plan to rule all of Greece
He raised a great army and made war on the other states
He built a new capital city in Laconia

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Spartans do a few days after receiving Philip's letter?
options: They sent back an answer of a single word
They sent Philip a formal declaration of war
They asked other states to help them decide
They ignored the letter completely

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might Philip's letter have seemed especially threatening?
options: He had never won a single battle before
He offered to share power with the Spartans
He asked the Spartans to name their own price for peace
He had already forced nearly every other Greek state to call him king

questions.prompt: As the passage explains it, what does "laconic" mean?
options: Speaking loudly enough to be heard from far away
Using as few words as possible to say something
Refusing to answer a question at all
Writing in a foreign alphabet

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Philip of Macedon is defeated in battle by the Spartans
Greece unites under Philip without any resistance
Sparta answers a Macedonian king's threat with a single, defiant word
The Spartans send Philip a long letter of surrender
